topic.name: Moments and Centers of Mass of Plane Laminas

question.text: The lamina $D = \big\{ (x,y) \: : \: 0 \le y \le x, \: 0 \le x \le 1 \big\}$ has the mass density function $\lambda(x,y)=3xy.$ Find the moment of the lamina about the $x$-axis.
question.explanation:
The moment of a lamina $D$ with the mass density function $\lambda(x,y)$ about the $x$-axis is given by

\[ M_x = \iint\limits_D y \, \lambda(x,y) \: \textrm{d}A. \]

In our case, $D$ is represented as a type I plane region and $\lambda(x,y) = 3xy.$

Therefore, the moment is

\begin{align*} M_x & = \iint\limits_D y \cdot 3xy \: \textrm{d}A \\[5pt] & = \iint\limits_D 3xy^2 \: \textrm{d}A \\[5pt] & = \int_{0}^{1} \int_{0}^{x} 3xy^2 \: \textrm{d}y \: \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] & = \int_{0}^{1} x\cdot \left[y^3\right]_{y=0}^{y=x} \: \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] & = \int_{0}^{1} x\cdot x^3 \: \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] & = \int_{0}^{1} x^4 \: \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &=\left[\dfrac15 x^5\right]_{x=0}^{x=1} \\[5pt] &=\dfrac15. \end{align*}

example.title: The Moment of a Plane Lamina About the X-Axis

question.text: The lamina $D = \big\{ (x,y) \: : \: 0 \le x \le 1,\, x^2 \le y \le 1 \big\}$ has the mass density function $\lambda(x,y)=\dfrac{15x^2}{y}.$ Find the moment of the lamina about the $x$-axis.
question.explanation:
The moment of a lamina $D$ with the mass density function $\lambda(x,y)$ about the $x$-axis is given by

\[ M_x = \iint\limits_D y \, \lambda(x,y) \: \textrm{d}A. \]

In our case, $D$ is represented as a type I plane region and $\lambda(x,y) = \dfrac{15x^2}{y}.$

Therefore, the moment is

\begin{align*} M_x & = \iint\limits_D y \cdot \dfrac{15x^2}{y} \: \textrm{d}A \\[5pt] & = \iint\limits_D 15x^2 \: \textrm{d}A \\[5pt] & = \int_{0}^{1} \int_{x^2}^{1}15x^2\: \textrm{d}y \: \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] & = \int_{0}^{1} 15x^2 \left[\int_{x^2}^{1}\: \textrm{d}y\right] \: \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] & = \int_{0}^{1} 15x^2\cdot \big[y\big]_{y=x^2}^{y=1} \: \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] & = \int_{0}^{1} 15x^2\cdot (1-x^2) \: \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] & = \int_{0}^{1}15x^2-15x^4 \: \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &=\left[5x^3 - 3x^5\right]_{x=0}^{x=1} \\[5pt] &=2. \end{align*}

example.title: The Moment of a Plane Lamina About the X-Axis

question.text: The lamina $D = \left\{ (x,y) \: : \: 0 \le x \le \dfrac{\pi}{2},\, 0 \le y \le \sin x \right\}$ has the mass density function $\lambda(x,y)=3y\cos x.$ Find the moment of the lamina about the $x$-axis.
question.explanation:
The moment of a lamina $D$ with the mass density function $\lambda(x,y)$ about the $x$-axis is given by

\[ M_x = \iint\limits_D y \, \lambda(x,y) \: \textrm{d}A. \]

In our case, $D$ is represented as a type I plane region and $\lambda(x,y) = 3y\cos x.$

Therefore, the moment is

\begin{align*} M_x & = \iint\limits_D y \cdot 3y\cos x \: \textrm{d}A \\[5pt] & = \iint\limits_D 3y^2\cos x \: \textrm{d}A \\[5pt] & = \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \int_{0}^{\sin x} 3y^2\cos x\: \textrm{d}y \: \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] & = \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \cos x \left[\int_{0}^{\sin x} 3y^2\: \textrm{d}y\right] \: \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] & = \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \cos x \cdot \left[y^3\right]_{y=0}^{y=\sin x} \: \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] & = \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \sin^3 x \cos x \: \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &=\left[\dfrac{\sin^4 x}{4}\right]_{x=0}^{x=\pi/2} \\[5pt] &=\dfrac14. \end{align*}

example.title: The Moment of a Plane Lamina About the X-Axis

question.text: The lamina $D = \left\{ (x,y) \: : \: \dfrac{1}{2} \le x \le 1 ,\, \ln x \le y \le 0 \right\}$ has the mass density function $\lambda(x,y)=2e^y.$ Find the moment of the lamina about the $y$-axis.
question.explanation:
The moment of a lamina $D$ with the mass density function $\lambda(x,y)$ about the $y$-axis is given by

\[ M_y = \iint\limits_D x \, \lambda(x,y) \: \textrm{d}A. \]

In our case, $D$ is represented as a type I plane region and $\lambda(x,y) = 2e^y.$

Therefore, the moment is

\begin{align*} M_y & = \iint\limits_D x \cdot 2e^y\: \textrm{d}A \\[5pt] & = \iint\limits_D 2 xe^y\: \textrm{d}A \\[5pt] & = \int_{1/2}^{1} \int_{\ln x}^{0} 2xe^y \: \textrm{d}y \: \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] & = \int_{1/2}^{1} 2x \left[ \int_{\ln x}^{0} e^y \: \textrm{d}y \right] \: \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] & = \int_{1/2}^{1} 2x\cdot \big[e^y\big]_{y=\ln x}^{y=0} \: \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] & = \int_{1/2}^{1} 2x(1-x)\: \textrm{d} x \\[5pt] & = \int_{1/2}^{1} 2x-2x^2 \: \textrm{d} x \\[5pt] &= \left[x^2 - \dfrac{2x^3}{3} \right]_{x=1/2}^{x=1} \\[5pt] &= \left(1 - \dfrac{2}{3} \right) - \left( \dfrac{1}{4} - \dfrac{1}{12} \right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{6} . \end{align*}

example.title: The Moment of a Plane Lamina About the Y-Axis

question.text: The lamina $D = \left\{ (x,y) \: : \: y^2 \le x \le 1 ,\, \dfrac{1}{2} \le y \le 1 \right\}$ has the mass density function $\lambda(x,y)=\dfrac{1}{x}.$ Find the moment of the lamina about the $y$-axis.
question.explanation:
The moment of a lamina $D$ with the mass density function $\lambda(x,y)$ about the $y$-axis is given by

\[ M_y = \iint\limits_D x \, \lambda(x,y) \: \textrm{d}A. \]

In our case, $D$ is represented as a type II plane region and $\lambda(x,y) =\dfrac{1}{x}.$

Therefore, the moment is

\begin{align*} M_y &= \iint\limits_D x \cdot \dfrac{1}{x} \: \textrm{d}A \\[5pt] &= \iint\limits_D 1 \: \textrm{d}A \\[5pt] &= \int_{1/2}^{1} \int_{y^2}^{1} \: \textrm{d}x \: \textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \int_{1/2}^{1} \big[ x\big]_{x=y^2}^{x=1} \: \textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \int_{1/2}^{1} 1-y^2 \: \textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \left[y - \dfrac{y^3}{3} \right]_{y=1/2}^{y=1} \\[5pt] &= \left(1-\dfrac{1}{3}\right) -\left(\dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{1}{24}\right) \\[5pt] &=\dfrac{5}{24}. \end{align*}
